thread:
Aisha (Security): Rolling out RBAC tightening for keystore SAs tomorrow 2026-06-12 14:00 UTC. Main change: remove legacy project-wide kms:Decrypt and replace with cryptoKey-level roles or key aliases. This is to reduce blast radius across regions.

Ben (Infra): Do we have a canonical mapping of clusters -> key aliases? Need to make sure proxies call the right alias/version.

Aisha (Security): Yes, mapping doc is in the infra repo under infra/keystore/alias-map.md. Short summary: prod clusters use aliases named projects/redwood-prod/.../cryptoKeys/keystore-key/cryptoKeyVersions/alias-<region>. We'll attach the mapping link in the rollout PR.

Carmen (SRE): Any expected mTLS client cert impact? Last time an SA permission issue caused handshake failures because the service couldn't decrypt its own private blob.

Aisha (Security): It can surface as handshake failures if the keystore can't decrypt TLS private keys or session ticket keys. We'll monitor handshake_fail_rate (service.proxy.handshake_failures) and KMS Deny logs. Rollout strategy: canary in us-central1 (5 nodes) then region rollouts. Pause criteria: if handshake_fail_rate >0.4% sustained for 4m, or >0.8% any 1m spike.

Diego (Platform): We'll add a pre-check job that validates each instance's SA has access to the target alias before changing bindings. Can we get a list of SAs to validate?

Aisha (Security): I'll export the SA list. Also plan to temporarily enable advanced audit logging (higher sampling) for key operations during the 2h window. That will help triage rapidly.

Eve (Oncall): Please post the exact logging queries. I'll wire them into the runbook so responders can copy/paste.

Aisha (Security): KMS Deny query (GCP):

```
resource.type="k8s_container"
logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/keystore-audit"
jsonPayload.methodName:"cloudkms.keys.decrypt"
jsonPayload.status.code=7
```

and to attribute to SA:

```
jsonPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="service-account@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```

Use gcloud logging read for quick checks: `gcloud logging read 'logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/keystore-audit" AND jsonPayload.methodName="cloudkms.keys.decrypt" AND jsonPayload.status.code=7' --freshness=1h`

infra-bot: scheduled pre-check job created: keystore-rbac-preflight-us-central1

Ben (Infra): Running the preflight now against canary. Found 2 pods referencing the old key alias name and one deployment using the legacy SA name in env var.

Carmen (SRE): I'm seeing a small uptick in handshake_failures in us-central1 at 13:52 UTC (0.45% over 5m). This is during preflight, not the RBAC apply. Any chance the preflight touches IAM?

Diego (Platform): Preflight only queries IAM and KMS via readonly APIs, shouldn't change bindings. Possibly stale cache in the keystore agent causing transient metrics. Carmen can you dump the agent logs?

Carmen (SRE): agent logs show repeated "decrypt: PERMISSION_DENIED" on one node 13:51:28Z. Attached snippet: `2026-06-12T13:51:28Z keystore-agent [WARN] decrypt failed: PERMISSION_DENIED principal=service-account-canary@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

Aisha (Security): That's expected for nodes still using old permissions. For mitigation: we have two safe options: (1) temporarily add cryptoKeyDecrypter role to the canary SA for that region with time-limited grant, or (2) patch keystore-agent to use a fallback cached key for 60s and exponential retry. Prefer (2) where feasible.

Ben (Infra): I'll stage the time-limited binding for the single affected SA to minimize blast radius. Will post the command and the audit link.

Eve (Oncall): If you stage binding, add TTL 30m and note the principal in runbook. Also trigger an alert rule that notifies security when a temporary grant is created.

Aisha (Security): Example gcloud to add binding (time-limited via org policy scheduled revoke):

```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding keystore-key \
  --location=us-central1 --keyring=keystore-prod \
  --member="serviceAccount:service-account-canary@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```

Remember to record the policy change and link it in the incident doc.

infra-bot: temp binding created by Ben for service-account-canary@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com (audit: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query; timewindow=now-1h)

Carmen (SRE): After the temp binding, decrypt errors dropped and handshake_fail_rate returned to baseline. I'll mark the canary healthy.

Diego (Platform): Next steps: (1) Diego to add pre-deploy check to fail rollout when any pod reports decrypt PERMISSION_DENIED in last 5m; (2) Aisha to finalize alias mapping PR and rollout schedule; (3) Ben to automate creation of time-limited bindings via terraform/rbac-ci for emergencies; (4) Eve to update runbook and add logging snippets.

Participants acked by emoji.

Aisha (Security): One more item: KMS key rotation compatibility. When we rotate keys, ensure alias mapping and SA grants are updated atomically. We'll test rotation in staging next week and include the postmortem template for any handshake regressions.

Eve (Oncall): I'll prep the postmortem template and include fields: SA affected, key alias, region, rollback actions, timeline, and audit links.

Ben (Infra): I'll open the infra PR for the alias mapping changes and include the preflight output for reviewers.

Diego (Platform): Scheduling a sync for 12:30 UTC tomorrow to confirm prechecks green. If any sustained decrypt denies during rollout -> stop and open incident channel inc-ks-20260612.

Aisha (Security): Thanks team. If you find any services that can't be migrated cleanly, escalate to security immediately.

Carmen (SRE): noted and will attach logs to the PR for visibility.
